column1: # boru Language Specification: type-system edge cases 1 — newtype
# symmetry + predicate subset symmetry
# Format: input<TAB>expected<TAB>description
# Companion to user-types.tsv. Pins the REFINE-NEWTYPE-VS-SUBSET
# decision (design/REFINE-NEWTYPE-VS-SUBSET.10.md) at EVERY boundary a
# value can cross — fn param, fn return, `is`, typed def, make, class
# field (make AND set) — with positive and negative rows per family.
#   - bare refine  → NEWTYPE: nominal, explicit construction, symmetric
#   - predicate refine → SUBSET: value-sensitive, no construction, symmetric
# Runs against the production lang registry (test/go/langspec).
# §1  a bare refine is a NEWTYPE — a raw base value is NOT a member
#     at ANY boundary (is / param / return / class field, make + set)
def P (refine Integer) 7 is P
column3: raw Integer is not a P at `is`

column1: def P (refine Integer) def g fn [[n:P] [Integer] [n add 1]] 7 g
column3: raw Integer rejected at a P param

column1: # (dropped) predicate/newtype-return type_error caught via do/error compiles-declines (falls back sound); semantics pinned by user-types.tsv + TestPredicateGuardNarrowing
def P (refine Integer) def S class {x:(make P 1)} make S {x:7}
column3: raw Integer rejected at a P-typed class field (make)

column1: # (dropped) P-typed class-field set rejection — same disposition as :22
def P (refine Integer) def S class {x:(make P 1)} (make S {}) dot x typeof
column3: the tagged default fills the field AND declares its type

column1: # §2  explicit construction — `def x:P v` and `make P v` both tag
def P (refine Integer) def x:P 42 x
column3: typed def constructs a P carrying the base value

column1: def P (refine Integer) def x:P 42 x typeof
column3: the constructed value carries the P tag

column1: def P (refine Integer) make P 42
column3: make on a newtype is the constructor twin of the typed def

column1: def P (refine Integer) (make P 42) is P
column3: a made P is a member

column1: def P (refine Integer) (make P '42') typeof
column3: make casts to the base first (String → Integer), then tags

column1: def P (refine Integer) do [make P 'zz'] error [dot code]
column3: an uncastable body is a loud make error (type_error), not a silent bind

column1: def P (refine Integer) def x:P 'hi'
column3: typed-def construction rejects a wrong-family body

column1: def P (refine Integer) def g fn [[n:P] [Integer] [n add 1]] (make P 7) g
column3: a made P dispatches at a P param, symmetric with def x:P

column1: def P (refine Integer) def mk fn [[] [P] [make P 5]] mk
column3: construction inside the body satisfies the P return

column1: def P (refine Integer) def mk fn [[] [P] [make P 5]] (mk) typeof
column3: the returned value still carries the tag

column1: def P (refine Integer) def x:P 42 x add 1
column3: arithmetic reads through the tag to the base value

column1: def P (refine Integer) def x:P 42 (x add 1) typeof
column3: …but the RESULT is a plain base value — ops do not preserve the tag

column1: def P (refine Integer) def x:P 42 x eq 42
column3: eq compares through the tag — a P 42 equals a raw 42

column1: # §3  sibling newtypes never mix — same base, distinct identities
def P (refine Integer) def Q (refine Integer) (make P 1) is Q
column3: a made P is not a sibling Q

column1: def P (refine Integer) def Q (refine Integer) def g fn [[n:Q] [Integer] [1]] def x:P 1 x g
column3: a P value is rejected at a Q param

column1: def P (refine Integer) def Q (refine Integer) def mk fn [[] [Q] [def x:P 1 x]] mk
column2: ERROR:return value 1: expected Q, got P
column3: a P value is rejected at a Q return — the error names both tags

column1: # (A computed body re-binds across siblings by re-tagging — `def b:Q
# (make P 1)` constructs a Q, typeof b = Q, b is P = false — but the
# dynamic-reparent typed-def shape is interpreter-only today, so those
# rows are not pinned here.)
# §4  a newtype OF a newtype — the nominal chain P ≤ Q widens up, never down
def P (refine Integer) def Q (refine P) def y:Q 3 y is Q
column3: a constructed Q is a Q

column1: def P (refine Integer) def Q (refine P) def y:Q 3 y is P
column3: …and widens one level to P

column1: def P (refine Integer) def Q (refine P) def y:Q 3 y is Integer
column3: …and to the base

column1: def P (refine Integer) def Q (refine P) def y:Q 3 y is Number
column3: …and on up the lattice

column1: def P (refine Integer) def Q (refine P) def y:Q 3 y typeof
column3: typeof names the innermost tag

column1: def P (refine Integer) def Q (refine P) def x:P 3 x is Q
column3: the supertype value is NOT the subtype

column1: def P (refine Integer) def Q (refine P) 3 is Q
column3: a raw base value is not a Q two mints down either

column1: def P (refine Integer) def Q (refine P) (make Q 3) is P
column3: make on the inner newtype widens the same way

column1: def P (refine Integer) def Q (refine P) def g fn [[n:P] [Integer] [7]] def y:Q 3 y g
column3: a Q value dispatches at a P param (subtype admitted)

column1: def P (refine Integer) def Q (refine P) def g fn [[n:Q] [Integer] [7]] def x:P 3 x g
column3: a P value is rejected at a Q param (supertype declined)

column1: def P (refine Integer) def Q (refine P) def mk fn [[] [P] [def y:Q 1 y]] mk
column3: a Q value satisfies a P return (subtype return)

column1: def P (refine Integer) def Q (refine P) def mk fn [[] [P] [def y:Q 1 y]] (mk) typeof
column3: …and keeps its own Q tag through the boundary

column1: # §5  newtypes over the other scalar families — same rules everywhere
def N (refine String) 'Ada' is N
column3: raw String is not an N (String-based newtype)

column1: def N (refine String) def x:N 'Ada' x is N
column3: a constructed N is a member

column1: def N (refine String) def x:N 'Ada' x is String
column3: …and widens to the String family

column1: def N (refine String) def x:N 'Ada' x is Integer
column3: tags widen up, not sideways

column1: def B (refine Boolean) true is B
column3: raw Boolean is not a B (Boolean-based newtype)

column1: def B (refine Boolean) def g fn [[b:B] [Integer] [1]] true g
column3: raw true rejected at a B param

column1: def B (refine Boolean) def g fn [[b:B] [Integer] [1]] def x:B true x g
column3: a constructed B dispatches

column1: def B (refine Boolean) def x:B true x is Boolean
column3: …and widens to the Boolean family

column1: def F (refine Float) def mk fn [[] [F] [def x:F 1.5 x]] mk
column3: a constructed F satisfies the F return (a raw 1.5 would be rejected — newtype strictness, §1)

column1: def P (refine Integer) def Q (refine P) (make Q '7') typeof
column3: make on an inner newtype casts to the ROOT base then tags with the inner mint

column1: # §6  undef + re-binding — the name goes away, live values keep their tag,
#     and the retired NAME cannot be re-minted
def P (refine Integer) undef P 7 is P
column3: after undef the name is gone from `is`

column1: def P (refine Integer) undef P make P 1
column3: …and from construction

column1: def P (refine Integer) def x:P 1 undef P x typeof
column3: a live value keeps its type identity after undef

column1: def P (refine Integer) def x:P 1 undef P x
column3: …and its value

column1: def P (refine Integer) undef P def P (refine Integer) 1
column2: ERROR:conflicts with an existing type name
column3: re-defining the SAME name after undef is a loud conflict (the retired node keeps the name)

column1: def P (refine Integer) undef P def P2 (refine Integer) def y:P2 1 y is P2
column3: a FRESH name mints fine after the undef

column1: def Big (Integer gt 10) undef Big 50 is Big
column3: predicate refinements undef the same way

column1: def Big (Integer gt 10) def b:Big 50 undef Big b
column3: a bound subset value survives its type's undef

column1: # §7  predicate refinements are SUBSET types — value-sensitive and
#     symmetric at param / return / bind / is, per predicate kind
# gte — boundary value belongs (contrast gt, user-types.tsv §4)
def Big (Integer gte 10) 10 is Big
column3: gte admits the boundary value

column1: def Big (Integer gte 10) 9 is Big
column3: …and rejects just below it

column1: def Big (Integer gte 10) def g fn [[n:Big] [Integer] [n]] 10 g
column3: gte boundary dispatches at the param

column1: def Big (Integer gte 10) def mk fn [[] [Big] [10]] (mk) eq 10
column3: …and is admitted at the return, value intact

column1: def Big (Integer gte 10) def b:Big 10 b
column3: …and at the bind

column1: def Sm (Integer lte 0) 0 is Sm
column3: lte admits the boundary value

column1: def Sm (Integer lte 0) 1 is Sm
column3: …and rejects just above it

column1: def Sm (Integer lte 0) def mk fn [[] [Sm] [-3]] (mk) eq -3
column3: lte return admits a satisfying value

column1: def Sm (Integer lte 0) def b:Sm 0 b
column3: lte bind admits its boundary

column1: # gt — the RETURN boundary is exactly as strict as the param
def Big (Integer gt 10) def mk fn [[] [Big] [11]] (mk) eq 11
column3: gt return admits the first passing value

column1: # (dropped) gt-return boundary rejection — same disposition as :22
# bind — `def b:Big v` runs the same predicate at bind time
def Big (Integer gt 10) def b:Big 11 b
column3: bind admits the first passing value

column1: def Big (Integer gt 10) def b:Big 10
column3: bind rejects the boundary value

column1: def Big (Integer gt 10) def b:Big 5
column3: bind rejects a deep miss

column1: # a subset value keeps its BASE tag — no reparenting (contrast §2 newtypes)
def Big (Integer gt 10) def b:Big 50 b typeof
column3: a bound subset value keeps the base tag

column1: def Big (Integer gt 10) def b:Big 50 b is Big
column3: …while remaining a member by value

column1: def Big (Integer gt 10) def b:Big 50 b is Integer
column3: …and a plain Integer

column1: # cross-family strictness — the base family gates before the predicate
def Big (Integer gt 10) 10.5 is Big
column3: a Float is not an Integer-refinement member even though 10.5 > 10

column1: def Big (Integer gt 10) def g fn [[n:Big] [Integer] [n]] 10.5 g
column3: …and is rejected at the param the same way

column1: # String base family
def S (String gt 'm') 'n' is S
column3: String predicate admits above the bound

column1: def S (String gt 'm') 'm' is S
column3: …and rejects the boundary (strict gt)

column1: def S (String gt 'm') def g fn [[s:S] [Integer] [1]] 'z' g
column3: String predicate param admits

column1: def S (String gt 'm') def g fn [[s:S] [Integer] [1]] 'a' g
column3: …and rejects

column1: def S (String gt 'm') def mk fn [[] [S] ['z']] (mk) eq 'z'
column3: String predicate return admits

column1: # (dropped) String-subset return rejection — same disposition as :22
def S (String gt 'm') def b:S 'z' b
column3: String predicate bind admits

column1: def S (String gt 'm') def b:S 'a'
column3: …and rejects

column1: # Float base family
def F (Float gte 0.0) def g fn [[f:F] [Float] [f]] 0.0 g
column3: Float gte admits its boundary at the param

column1: def F (Float gte 0.0) def mk fn [[] [F] [2.5]] (mk) eq 2.5
column3: Float predicate return admits

column1: def F (Float gte 0.0) def b:F 0.0 b
column3: Float predicate bind admits the boundary

column1: def F (Float gte 0.0) def b:F -0.5
column3: Float predicate bind rejects

column1: def F (Float gt 1.5) 2 is F
column3: an Integer is not a member of a Float refinement (strict leaves)

column1: # between — closed interval, both ends in
def R (Integer between 10 20) 10 is R
column3: between includes the low end

column1: def R (Integer between 10 20) 20 is R
column3: …and the high end

column1: def R (Integer between 10 20) 9 is R
column3: below the interval

column1: def R (Integer between 10 20) 21 is R
column3: above the interval

column1: def R (Integer between 10 20) def g fn [[n:R] [Integer] [n]] 15 g
column3: between param admits an interior value

column1: def R (Integer between 10 20) def g fn [[n:R] [Integer] [n]] 25 g
column3: …and rejects an exterior one

column1: def R (Integer between 10 20) def mk fn [[] [R] [15]] (mk) eq 15
column3: between return admits

column1: def R (Integer between 10 20) def b:R 20 b
column3: between bind admits the closed high end

column1: def R (Integer between 10 20) def b:R 21
column3: …and rejects just past it

column1: # §8  conjunctive refinement — the meet (tand / unify) intersects
#     interval predicates; BOTH bounds always apply
def Big (Integer gt 10) def W (Big tand (Integer lt 20)) W
column3: tand on a named refinement meets to the interval intersection, recorded as W's content — the NAME renders (§6); the bounds are pinned by `def w:W 15` rows

column1: def Big (Integer gt 10) def W (Big tand (Integer lt 20)) 11 is W
column3: interior value, low side

column1: def Big (Integer gt 10) def W (Big tand (Integer lt 20)) 19 is W
column3: interior value, high side

column1: def Big (Integer gt 10) def W (Big tand (Integer lt 20)) 10 is W
column3: Big's strict low bound still applies

column1: def Big (Integer gt 10) def W (Big tand (Integer lt 20)) 20 is W
column3: the added strict high bound applies too

column1: def Big (Integer gt 10) def W (Big tand (Integer lt 20)) 3 is W
column3: a deep miss on the inherited bound — Big's constraint is never lost in the meet

column1: def Big (Integer gt 10) def W (Big tand (Integer lt 20)) 25 is W
column3: …nor is the new one

column1: def Big (Integer gt 10) def W (Big tand (Integer lt 20)) def g fn [[n:W] [Integer] [n]] 15 g
column3: the meet type dispatches like any refinement

column1: def Big (Integer gt 10) def W (Big tand (Integer lt 20)) def g fn [[n:W] [Integer] [n]] 25 g
column3: …and rejects at the param

column1: def Big (Integer gt 10) def W (Big tand (Integer lt 20)) def mk fn [[] [W] [15]] (mk) eq 15
column3: …admits at the return (both bounds hold)

column1: def Big (Integer gt 10) def W (Big tand (Integer lt 20)) def w:W 15 w
column3: …binds a passing literal

column1: def Big (Integer gt 10) def W (Big tand (Integer lt 20)) def w:W 5
column3: …and rejects a failing one at bind

column1: # disjoint intervals — the meet is EMPTY, spelled Never
def Big (Integer gt 10) def W (Big tand (Integer lt 5)) W
column3: a disjoint meet folds to Never

column1: def Big (Integer gt 10) def W (Big tand (Integer lt 5)) 3 is W
column3: nothing inhabits the empty meet — not even a value passing ONE side

column1: def Big (Integer gt 10) def W (Big tand (Integer lt 5)) 12 is W
column3: …nor the other

column1: def A (Integer gt 10) def B (Integer lt 5) A unify B
column3: unify reports the empty intersection as a failure

column1: def A (Integer gt 10) def B (Integer lt 5) def x:(A tand B) 3
column2: ERROR:does not unify with declared type Never
column3: binding at the empty meet is a loud unify error naming Never

column1: # cross-family meets are empty too
def Big (Integer gt 10) Big tand String
column3: an Integer refinement meets String at Never

column1: def Big (Integer gt 10) def W (Big tand (String gt 'm')) W
column3: …including String's own refinements

column1: # meets chain — three constraints intersect pairwise
((Integer gt 0) tand (Integer lt 100)) tand (Integer gt 50)
column3: a chained meet keeps the tightest bound per side

column1: # §9  validate-then-call — an `is` guard proves membership at runtime,
#     so the guarded branch dispatches and the other branch never errors
# (dropped) validate-then-call `if (x is Big) [g x]` runs correct but compile-declines (guard narrowing is a CHECK win, not compile coverage); pinned by TestPredicateGuardNarrowing
def Big (Integer gt 10) def g fn [[n:Big] [Integer] [n]] def x 50 if (x is (tnot Big)) [0] [g x]
column3: the complement guard flips the branches — else proves membership

column1: def P (refine Integer) def g fn [[n:P] [Integer] [n add 1]] def h fn [[v:Integer] [Integer] [if (v is P) [g v] [0]]] h 5
column3: newtype guard, false side: a raw base value takes the else branch instead of the call erroring

column1: def P (refine Integer) def g fn [[n:P] [Integer] [n add 1]] def h fn [[v:Integer] [Integer] [if (v is P) [g v] [0]]] def x:P 5 h x
column3: …and a constructed value passes guard AND call through the same wrapper
